title: How Greg would grow an AI SaaS to $100k/month with no team using affiliates and gamification
summary: Greg lays out a zero-to-$100k/month SaaS playbook: pick a niche you understand, prototype with AI coding tools, then buy distribution with a 30-50% affiliate revenue share aimed at mid-sized creators. He layers on gamification, AI-driven product feedback and building in public to keep churn low and the business lean.

principles.text: Pick a niche you deeply understand and write one positioning sentence: help X do painful Y in 10 minutes instead of 10 hours.
principles.quote: I help [this person] do [this painful thing] in 10 minutes instead of 10 hours.” That becomes the positioning.

principles.text: Talk to about 5 people in the niche before building, to learn where they spend time and money.
principles.quote: I’d talk to 5 of them, figure out where they spend time and money, and write down one sentence

principles.text: Trade margin for distribution: offer a very high affiliate revenue share early, then lower it for later affiliates.
principles.quote: I’d happily give up 30 to 50 percent to build momentum. Most people think that’s too high. But they’re thinking short-term. You’re trading margin for distribution.

principles.text: Go wide on B- and C-list creators (5k-70k followers) who have trust and aren't over-messaged, instead of chasing A-listers.
principles.quote: People with 5k to 70k followers who already have trust, aren’t over-messaged, and know their audience well.

principles.text: Make each affiliate pitch short and specific, with a personal 90-second Loom and a white-labeled dashboard.
principles.quote: I’d record a 90-second Loom for each one, showing exactly how it works, and set them up with a white-labeled affiliate dashboard.

principles.text: Build what users are already doing: use AI to mine complaints and stuck points, which keeps churn low and word of mouth high.
principles.quote: I build what’s already happening organically. That keeps churn low and word of mouth high.
